title: Switch statement basics
recap: A switch selects between several fixed alternatives by comparing one integral value against case labels. Each case runs until a break, and the default label catches every value without a matching case.
Switches express multi-way selection more clearly than a long if / else if chain when every branch tests the same value for equality.
objectives: Implement statusMessage from its behavioral contract.
Practice the lesson construct by writing the control flow yourself.
Handle multiple inputs and edge cases without hard-coded example answers.
warnings: The examples are not the whole test suite; implement the general behavior.
Do not edit the test drivers. Only the supplied public function signatures are fixed.
Console output and exact source tokens are not graded.
challenge: Implement statusMessage using a switch statement. Return "running" for 1, "paused" for 2, "stopped" for 3, and "unknown" for every other integer. Return the text; do not print it.
hints: Switch on the function parameter, not a fixed example.
Each case can return its result immediately.
Use default for all unrecognized values.
